the_day: Anthropic's amended IPO filing showed its revenue and spending commitments, OpenAI is changing how the ChatGPT apps are organized and cut back a funding round, xAI lowered Grok Bot usage limits because of cost, and Google had no new news.

items.headline: Anthropic's amended IPO filing shows $17 billion in quarterly revenue
points: Anthropic's amended IPO filing shows about $17 billion in third-quarter revenue, CNBC, AP and Bloomberg report.
It lists $895.4 billion in purchase commitments, CNBC reports, and CoinDesk says the quarter ended with a $567 million operating loss.
Fortune reports that growth slowed and costs jumped. Reuters says the filing plans a $3.5 billion share sale to investors in Japan.

items.headline: Claude Code now refuses to recreate existing video games
points: Anthropic has added a rule that stops Claude Code from recreating existing games, GamesIndustry.biz and The Verge report.
Tom's Hardware says Anthropic confirmed the new limits, and some users say Opus 5.5 is also blocking reverse engineering tasks.
HotHardware reports a mixed reaction from game developers.
items.for_you: Developers using Claude Code to build games may have requests refused if they closely copy an existing game.

items.headline: OpenAI retires ChatGPT Classic app and merges Chat and Work tabs
points: OpenAI is retiring the ChatGPT Classic app and replacing it with its desktop app, 9to5Mac and AppleInsider report.
ChatGPT's Chat and Work tabs will merge into one experience, TechCrunch and The Verge report.
MIXED reports OpenAI says Instant chat will not count against the ChatGPT and Codex usage allowance that both will share from December.

items.headline: OpenAI cuts funding round as Altman signs Abu Dhabi deals
points: OpenAI raised less than half of its $30 billion target in its latest funding round, the WSJ reports. CNBC says the goal was cut, citing sources.
Forbes reports the round is now $20 billion, with investors from the UAE putting in both money and computing capacity.
ADNOC and G42 signed a deal with OpenAI, Reuters reports. Energy Connects says ADNOC is the first energy company to use OpenAI Frontier.
